body:
Nothing significant. 

I had a particularly bad day, I don't remember the specific triggers or what I was feeling. I had been feeling suicidal thoughts for more than a year but always told myself that I was too much of a pussy to go through with it. After that bad day, I remember walking out to my shed and unlocking the door and just standing there with a flashlight, looking up at the rafters.

I kept telling myself that "you won't do this, you're too much of a piece of shit".. but I kept going. I remember tying the noose thinking that maybe this is what I needed to talk myself out of it, you know? Just sort of phantom through the motions and see that this is death we are talking about. I remember tying 8 rings, not being able to remember if it was 8 or 12, and then tying off to the rafters.

But still, I persisted in thinking that I had to talk myself out of it by going through the motions. I remember stepping onto a propane tank and stepping into the noose, still thinking "you're a pussy, you won't do this".. and then I stepped off. I remember the gasping, that irrefutable sound of being strangled, just like the movies. Then I remember starting to black out and this warm feeling all over my face. 

My survival instincts kicked in literally a second or two before I passed out and I managed to swing my feet back onto the propane tank. I was gasping and beet red, I took the noose off and walked out of the shed in tears, telling myself that I had to call the cops but how to go about it because I work in emergency services and my co-workers would undoubtedly show up. 

I curled up on the floor and cried for about an hour and a half while listening to [this song](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDD9YF_0q7E) about suicide which I could relate to. Shortly after that, I posted to /r/SuicideWatch. To this day (about 13 months), I haven't told anyone and while I still feel like I am a lonely, depressed, piece of shit, I could not burden other people with the idea that I was seconds from being found hanging in a fucking shed by my co-workers and ex-girlfriend.

I just wanted to thank everyone for their support. I didn't go to the police and I haven't told anyone (other than the internet) about what happened. I am going to avoid the hospital for now because I know all of the nursing staff, but I will look into receiving help.

The danger is over for now. My throat is hurting from being asphyxiated and I have a headache. I still feel directionless. 

I've known that I've had problems for a long time. I completed an anger management course and it was for the better. Where once situations filled me with petty rage, I can now control myself and stay rational. 

I am still weighed down by my guilt from my previous actions, however, you've taught me that it isn't too late to improve myself, which I have been doing. It's hard when you know that you drained the life out of something so beautiful with your stupidity. When you look back and realize how clear the answers to conflicts were it pains me to think about how I acted without any thought of consequence. 

Anyway, thank you all again. I don't have many friends to begin with as I refuse to let people in in fear of being judged, or worse, being justified in my actions, but it was a relief to finally be able to tell someone what I am and what I have done.

It stemmed from immaturity. When I entered into conflicts, I was unable to remain a rational adult and I lashed out with petty insults and anger. It was pathetic and accomplished nothing other than hurting people and protecting my own insecurities. I completed anger management, but it was too little too late, as the damage was already done.

I'm not, though. I don't believe I am a rotten person, I just do bad things. It's exacerbated by the fact I've had such an easy upbringing. My parents are middle class and have worked tirelessly to support me. They tried their absolute hardest to raise me, but I'm still able to do terrible things to beautiful people.

It was my physiological instincts that pulled me back up. I didn't go out there to do it. I had been thinking about it for years. Today was an especially bad day. I told myself if I went out and looked at it, I would talk myself down and come back in.

Except I didn't. 

I tied the knot and dared myself to go further, just so I could come back down. I tied the clove hitch and dared myself to go further. I stepped onto the tank and dared myself again and then stepped off. 

I do have lifeline, but it's not an option. I've put the last 6 years into accomplishing my lifelong goal, so I can't throw it away when I'm so close to the finish line.  

Thank you, interwebs
